title: Vector Emplace Back
description: Construct element in-place at end (more efficient than push_back)
explanation: Emplace constructs the element directly in the vector, avoiding a temporary copy.

title: Vector Emplace
description: Construct element in-place at a specific position
explanation: Similar to insert, but constructs the element in-place to avoid copies.

title: Vector Shrink To Fit
description: Reduce capacity to match size, freeing unused memory
explanation: Requests the vector to reduce its capacity to fit its size. Useful after removing many elements.

title: Vector Data Pointer
description: Get pointer to the underlying contiguous array
explanation: Returns a pointer to the internal memory buffer for C-style array interop.

title: Vector Max Size
description: Get the maximum possible number of elements
explanation: Returns the theoretical maximum size the vector can reach based on memory constraints.

title: Vector At With Bounds Checking
description: Access element with bounds checking (throws out_of_range)
explanation: Safe element access that throws std::out_of_range if the index is invalid.

title: Vector Assign
description: Assign new contents replacing current ones
explanation: Clears the vector and fills it with n copies of value, or from an iterator range.

title: Vector Erase With Std Erase C++20
description: Erase all elements matching a value (C++20 std::erase)
explanation: C++20 introduced std::erase and std::erase_if as a simpler alternative to the erase-remove idiom.

title: Vector Insert Range
description: Insert a range of elements at a position
explanation: Inserts all elements from another container (or initializer list) at a specified position.

title: Vector Bool Specialization
explanation: vector<bool> is a space-optimized specialization that stores bits, not bools. Access returns a proxy reference.

title: Vector With Custom Allocator
description: Use a custom allocator with vector
explanation: Vectors can use custom allocators for memory management control (pool, arena, etc.).

title: Vector Iterator Invalidation
description: Understand when vector iterators become invalid
explanation: Insertions/reallocations invalidate all iterators; erasures invalidate from the erase point onward.

title: Vector Reserve For Performance
description: Pre-allocate memory to avoid repeated reallocations
explanation: Reserving memory ahead of push_back calls avoids costly reallocations and copies.
